extracted.intended_audience: Federal agencies' EEO officers, agency counsel, complainants and their representatives (attorneys), and EEOC staff
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory standards and procedural requirements (29 CFR Part 1614) governing processing of federal-sector EEO complaints, attorney's fees and costs, compliance/enforcement of Commission decisions, data reporting under the No FEAR Act, and related matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presumption of entitlement to attorney's fees upon finding of discrimination
rubrics_metrics.description: A finding of discrimination raises a presumption of entitlement to an award of attorney's fees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any award of attorney's fees or costs shall be paid by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may receive attorney's fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorney's fees are allowable only for the services of members of the Bar and law clerks, paralegals or law students under the supervision of members of the Bar; no award is allowable for the services of any employee of the Federal Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This limits fee awards to private counsel and supervised non-attorney support, excluding federal employees' services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and notice requirements for attorney's fees
rubrics_metrics.description: Attorney's fees shall be paid for services performed by an attorney after the filing of a written complaint, provided the attorney provides reasonable notice of representation to the agency, administrative judge or Commission; fees may be allowable for a reasonable period prior to notification for services performed in reaching a determination to represent the complainant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies are not required to pay fees for pre-complaint services, except when the Commission affirms on appeal an administrative judge's discrimination finding after an agency took final action by not implementing the administrative judge's decision. Written submissions signed by the representative are deemed notice of representation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission contents and deadline for fee/cost claims
rubrics_metrics.description: When entitlement is determined, the complainant's attorney shall submit a verified statement of attorney's fees (including expert witness fees) and other costs to the agency or administrative judge within 30 days of receipt of the decision and provide a copy to the agency. The statement shall be accompanied by an affidavit itemizing the attorney's charges for legal services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency may respond within 30 days. The verified statement, affidavit, and any agency response become part of the complaint file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency/administrative judge decision on amount and appeal notice
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency or administrative judge shall issue a decision determining the amount of attorney's fees or costs due within 60 days of receipt of the statement and affidavit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision must include a notice of right to appeal to the EEOC (with EEOC Form 573) and specific reasons for determining the amount of the award.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard for calculating attorney's fees (lodestar)
rubrics_metrics.description: The amount of attorney's fees shall be calculated using the standard: the number of hours reasonably expended multiplied by a reasonable hourly rate as the starting point.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: There is a strong presumption that the lodestar represents the reasonable fee. In limited circumstances the amount may be reduced or increased based on degree of success, quality of representation, and long delay caused by the agency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of costs awardable (28 U.S.C. 1920)
rubrics_metrics.description: Costs that may be awarded include those authorized by 28 U.S.C. 1920: fees of the reporter for necessary stenographic transcripts; fees and disbursements for printing and witnesses; and fees for exemplification and copies necessarily obtained for use in the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expert witness fees are part of the verified statement; witness fees otherwise governed by 28 U.S.C. 1821 (see next criterion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Witness fee rules (28 U.S.C. 1821) and federal employee exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Witness fees shall be awarded in accordance with 28 U.S.C. 1821, except that no award shall be made for a Federal employee who is in a duty status when made available as a witness.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Federal employees who testify while in duty status are not entitled to witness fee awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory compliance with final Commission decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Relief ordered in a final Commission decision is mandatory and binding on the agency except as provided in the section; failure to implement ordered relief may be subject to judicial enforcement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See enforcement provisions (e.g., §1614.503(g)) for remedies when agencies do not comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temporary or conditional restoration pending reconsideration
rubrics_metrics.description: When an agency requests reconsideration and the case involves removal, separation, or suspension continuing beyond the request date, and the decision orders retroactive restoration, the agency shall comply to the extent of temporary or conditional restoration of the employee to duty status in the position specified, pending reconsideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service under temporary/conditional restoration is credited toward probationary/trial period, within-grade increases, or career tenure service if the Commission upholds its decision after reconsideration. The agency may delay payment of monetary amounts pending reconsideration but must pay interest if payment is later required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification requirement when relief is temporary/conditional
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall notify the Commission and the employee in writing at the same time it requests reconsideration that the relief it provides is temporary or conditional and, if applicable, that it will delay payment of any amounts owed but will pay interest as specified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to provide this notification will result in dismissal of the agency's request for reconsideration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deadline for providing relief when no reconsideration or denial
rubrics_metrics.description: When no request for reconsideration is filed or when a request for reconsideration is denied, the agency shall provide the relief ordered and there is no further right to delay implementation; relief shall be provided in full not later than 120 days after receipt of the final decision unless otherwise ordered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a mandatory implementation timeline for final Commission decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Petition for enforcement to the Office of Federal Operations
rubrics_metrics.description: A complainant may petition the Commission for enforcement of an appellate decision by submitting a petition to the Office of Federal Operations that specifically sets forth reasons supporting a belief that the agency is not complying with the decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The petition triggers agency fact-finding and Commission enforcement procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Office of Federal Operations compliance actions and clarification powers
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Federal Operations shall take action to ascertain whether the agency is implementing the Commission decision and undertake efforts to obtain compliance. It may, on its own motion or in response to enforcement petitions or timely reconsideration requests, issue clarifications of prior decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarifications may further explain meaning/intent but cannot change the result or enlarge/diminish relief ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral and Commission enforcement powers
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Director, Office of Federal Operations, cannot obtain satisfactory compliance, the Director shall submit findings/recommendations for enforcement to the Commission or refer the matter to another appropriate agency as directed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission may issue a notice to show cause to the head of the noncomplying agency, request appearances or written responses with evidence of compliance or compelling reasons for non-compliance, and may refer matters to the Office of Special Counsel when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to complainant of administrative completion and judicial rights
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the Commission has determined that an agency is not complying with a prior decision or has failed to submit required compliance reports, the Commission shall notify the complainant of the right to file a civil action for enforcement under Title VII, ADEA, Equal Pay Act, Rehabilitation Act, GINA, or PWFA, to seek judicial review under the APA and mandamus statute, or to commence de novo proceedings under appropriate statutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice informs complainants of available judicial and statutory enforcement options.

rubrics_metrics.name: Settlement agreements binding and noncompliance procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Any settlement agreement knowingly and voluntarily agreed to by the parties at any stage of the complaint process shall be binding on both parties; final agency action not appealed or litigated is binding on the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If complainant believes agency failed to comply with settlement terms, they must notify the EEO Director in writing within 30 days of when they knew or should have known; complainant may request specific implementation or reinstatement for further processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals regarding alleged noncompliance with settlements/decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: If dissatisfied with the agency's attempt to resolve alleged noncompliance, the complainant may appeal to the Commission: may file an appeal 35 days after serving the agency with allegations of noncompliance, but must file within 30 days of receipt of the agency's determination; must serve a copy on the agency; the agency may respond within 30 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior to determination, the Commission may request additional information or order an investigation/hearing and may order compliance or reinstatement if noncompliance is not attributable to the complainant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Processing subsequent acts of discrimination separately
rubrics_metrics.description: Allegations that subsequent acts of discrimination violate a settlement agreement shall be processed as separate complaints under the regular complaint processing sections, rather than under the settlement noncompliance section.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinct subsequent allegations are treated as new complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim relief when agency appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: When the agency appeals and the case involves removal/separation/suspension continuing beyond the date of the appeal and the AJ's decision orders retroactive restoration, the agency shall provide temporary/conditional restoration pending appeal; the employee may decline interim relief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Service under interim relief is credited if the Commission upholds the decision; if Commission reverses, credit does not apply. Agency may delay payments other than prospective pay and benefits pending appeal but must pay interest if payment later required. Agency must notify Commission/employee in writing when it appeals that relief is temporary/conditional; failure to notify results in dismissal of appeal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency may decline return if unduly disruptive
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency may, by notice to the complainant, decline to return the complainant to his or her place of employment if return would be unduly disruptive to the work environment, but prospective pay and benefits must be provided.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determination not to return the complainant is not reviewable. Interim relief does not insulate complainant from subsequent disciplinary/adverse action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Complainant's remedy if agency fails to provide required interim relief on appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: If the agency files an appeal and has not provided required interim relief, the complainant may request dismissal of the agency's appeal. The request must be filed with the Office of Federal Operations within 25 days of service of the agency's appeal and a copy served on the agency; the agency may respond within 15 days.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This provides a procedural remedy to compel interim relief when required.

rubrics_metrics.name: EEO group statistics system requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall establish a system to collect and maintain accurate employment information on the race, national origin, sex and disability of its employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data must be accurate and maintained per Commission-prescribed procedures and controls.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary self-identification and fallback procedures for demographic data
rubrics_metrics.description: Data on race, national origin and sex shall be collected by voluntary self-identification; if an employee does not voluntarily provide the information, the agency shall advise the employee of the importance and, if still refusing, make a visual identification and inform the employee of the data to be reported. If agency believes information is inaccurate, it shall advise the employee; if employee declines to change, agency must accept it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collection emphasizes voluntariness and sensitivity; the agency must communicate purpose and privacy protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on collection and disclosure of individual-level demographic data
rubrics_metrics.description: Information collected shall be disclosed only in the form of gross statistics; an agency shall not collect or maintain any information on the race, national origin or sex of individual employees except when an automated data processing system is used in accordance with Commission-prescribed standards to ensure individual privacy and separation from personnel records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protects individual privacy; exceptions allowed only under Commission standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Controls over agency EEO data systems
rubrics_metrics.description: Each system is subject to controls: (1) only Commission-prescribed categories of race/national origin may be used; (2) only Commission-prescribed/approved collection/maintenance procedures may be used; (3) the Commission shall review operation of agency systems for adherence; exceptions require advance written Commission approval.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures standardization and Commission oversight of demographic data collection systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted uses of EEO data and prohibition on quotas
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency may use the data only in studies and analyses that contribute affirmatively to achieving EEO program objectives; an agency shall not establish quotas for employment on the basis of race, color, religion, sex, or national origin.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Data use is limited to affirmative programmatic purposes, not for quota-setting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability data collection methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Data on disabilities shall be collected using methods permitted under specified sections (§1614.203(d)(6)(ii) and (iii)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Refer to cited sections for acceptable disability data collection procedures to ensure compliance with privacy and statutory requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency reporting obligations to the Commission
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency shall report to the Commission on employment by race, national origin, sex and disability in the form and at such times as the Commission may require.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must follow Commission's format and schedule for reporting demographic employment data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting to the Commission on pre-complaint counseling and complaint processing
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall report to the Commission information concerning pre-complaint counseling and the status, processing and disposition of complaints under this part at times and in the manner the Commission prescribes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must keep the Commission informed about counseling and complaint processing activity per Commission instructions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification to Commission of related Federal court complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall advise the Commission whenever it is served with a Federal court complaint based upon a complaint that is pending on appeal at the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures Commission awareness of parallel judicial proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual national and regional EEO plans requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall submit annually for Commission review and approval written national and regional EEO plans of action in a Commission-prescribed format that must include training/education program provisions, descriptions of qualifications of principal/operating EEO officials, and descriptions of personnel and resource allocations proposed to carry out the agency's EEO program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plans must be in the Commission's prescribed format and cover at least the listed elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable efforts to settle complaints early
rubrics_metrics.description: Each agency shall make reasonable efforts to voluntarily settle complaints of discrimination as early as possible in, and throughout, administrative processing, including the pre-complaint counseling stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any settlement reached must be in writing, signed by both parties, and identify the claims resolved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Time computation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All time periods stated in days are calendar days unless otherwise stated; a document is timely if received or postmarked before expiration, or if mailed within five days when no legible postmark; filings via EEOC Public Portal or FedSEP are deemed filed on upload date and timeliness determined by submitter's time zone.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: EEOC decisions transmitted via Portal/email deemed received when accessed or within five days of upload/email, whichever is earlier. Various procedural verbs include digital transmissions. Time limits subject to waiver, estoppel, and equitable tolling; first day counted is the day after the triggering event and last day is included unless it falls on a weekend/holiday (then extended to next business day).

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital transmission equivalence for filing/serving
rubrics_metrics.description: For specified sections, terms like accept, file, filed, filing, issue, notify, receive, serve, submission, transmit, etc., shall include digital transmissions made through FedSEP, the EEOC Public Portal, or by email.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This treats electronic filings and transmissions as equivalent to paper filings for timeliness and service purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to representation and official time
rubrics_metrics.description: At any stage, including counseling, the complainant has the right to be accompanied, represented, and advised by a representative of their choice. If the complainant or their designated representative is an agency employee, they shall have a reasonable amount of official time, if otherwise on duty, to prepare/respond; witnesses who are Federal employees shall be in duty status when presence is authorized or required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The agency is not required to change schedules, incur overtime, or pay travel to facilitate a specific representative. When an attorney is designated, official correspondence is served on the attorney and complainant and timeframes are computed from the attorney's receipt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disqualification of representatives for conflicts
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases where representation would conflict with the official or collateral duties of the representative, the Commission or the agency may, after giving the representative an opportunity to respond, disqualify the representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures that individuals with conflicting duties are not permitted to represent parties in a complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correspondence service after designation of representative
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless the complainant states otherwise in writing, after the agency has received written notice of the name, address and telephone number of a representative for the complainant, all official correspondence shall be with the representative with copies to the complainant. The complainant must serve all official correspondence on the designated representative of the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an attorney is representative, service to the attorney triggers timelines; complainant remains responsible for proceeding with the complaint.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consolidation/joint processing of complaints
rubrics_metrics.description: Complaints filed by two or more complainants with substantially similar allegations or relating to the same matter may be consolidated by the agency or Commission after appropriate notification. Two or more complaints by the same complainant shall be consolidated by the agency after notice. When consolidated with earlier complaints, the agency shall complete investigation within the earlier of 180 days after filing the last complaint or 360 days after filing the original complaint, except complainant may request a hearing any time after 180 days from the first-filed complaint.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative judges or the Commission may consolidate multiple complaints by the same complainant in their discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delegation of authority by agency heads
rubrics_metrics.description: An agency head may delegate authority under this part to one or more designees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows agencies to assign operational authority to appropriate officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and scope of No FEAR Act subpart
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart implements Title III of the No FEAR Act and sets forth basic responsibilities of Federal agencies and the Commission to post certain information on their public websites.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establishes the web-posting and reporting duties imposed by the No FEAR Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Key definitions for data posting and process steps
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions provided include: Federal agency; Commission; investigation; hearing; without a hearing; after a hearing; final action by an agency; final action involving a finding of discrimination; appeal; basis of alleged discrimination (list of protected bases); issue of alleged discrimination (EEOC Standard Form 462 categories); subordinate component (organizational sub-unit with 1,000+ employees required to submit EEOC Form 715-01).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These definitions are authoritative for interpreting posting and reporting requirements under the subpart.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manner and format of No FEAR Act data postings
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall post statistical data in PDF and an accessible text format that complies with Section 508; prominently post the date of last update; include separate data for each subordinate component identified as pertaining to that component; title data as specified and post a 'No FEAR Act Data' hyperlink on agency homepage (and subordinate component homepages where applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies with 100+ employees and subordinate component data must use EEOC's prescribed template. Agencies may not post separate quarterly statistics for the current fiscal year (only cumulative). Ensure data are accessible via commercial search engines. Provide the Commission the data URL within 60 days of the rule's effective date and update URL changes within 30 days. Processing times must be recorded using number of days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Layout and ordering requirements for posted data
rubrics_metrics.description: Cumulative quarterly and fiscal year data shall appear in vertical columns (oldest fiscal year left to right), categories in horizontal rows in the same order as §1614.704(a)-(m). When posting bases and issues, those shall be arranged in the order they appear in the definitions (§1614.702(j) and (k)), with 'non-EEO basis' posted last after 'disability'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensures uniform presentation across agencies; follow EEOC template where required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data accessibility requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall ensure the data they post under this subpart can be readily accessed through one or more commercial search engines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Promotes public discoverability of posted EEO statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quarterly posting schedule for current fiscal year data
rubrics_metrics.description: Commencing January 31, 2004 and thereafter no later than 30 days after the end of each fiscal quarter, each Federal agency shall post current fiscal year statistics on its public website regarding EEO complaints filed under part 1614 as specified in §1614.704.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quarterly posting ensures up-to-date public reporting of EEO complaint statistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required categories of No FEAR Act data to be posted (agency)
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies must post a set of specified statistics for the current fiscal year, including: number of complaints filed; number of individuals filing; number filing two or more; counts by basis and by issue (and non-EEO basis); average length of time to complete investigation and final action overall and separated by whether hearing was requested; number of complaints dismissed and average pendency prior to dismissal; number withdrawn; totals of final actions involving findings of discrimination and percentages rendered without/after hearing; breakdowns of those findings by basis and issue including percentages; counts and statuses of complaints filed before current fiscal year and pending at each process step; total number of complaints where investigation not completed within regulatory time requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each item (a)-(m) in §1614.704 is discrete and must be reported in the agency's posted data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comparative year-end data requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Commencing January 31, 2004 and thereafter no later than January 31 each year, agencies shall post year-end data corresponding to §1614.704 for each of the five immediately preceding fiscal years (or as many years as available), providing a separate figure for each fiscal year and category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides multi-year comparability for public review and trend analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on combining other data with required No FEAR Act data
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies shall not include or otherwise post any other data with the data required under §§1614.704 and 1614.705, though they may post other data on a separate web page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keeps the required dataset discrete and standard across agencies.

rubrics_metrics.name: EEOC posting requirements for hearing statistics
rubrics_metrics.description: The Commission shall post current fiscal year statistics regarding hearings requested under part 1614, including number of hearings requested, number of individuals filing, number filing two or more, counts of hearing requests by basis and issue, average length of time to complete the hearing step, and administrative judge (AJ) decisions rendered with findings of discrimination with breakdowns by hearing/no hearing and by basis.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mirrors agency posting requirements but applied to the Commission's hearing-step statistics; ensures transparency of AJ decision outcomes and hearing processing times.
